description:
FILED s470bm (Opus, 2026-09-05).  PRE-EXISTING.  Found by the Part B item B4
host-leak census (#1172) over perl's own t/ — the emitted token
`-norequire::plc--norequire` is not a name the IR declares, which is how it
surfaced.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s470bm/f13.pl):

    package Foo; sub hi { "hi" }
    package Bar; use parent qw( -norequire Foo );
    package main;
    print "ISA=[@Bar::ISA]\n";
    print "isa_foo=",  (Bar->isa("Foo")        ? 1 : 0), "\n";
    print "isa_nore=", (Bar->isa("-norequire") ? 1 : 0), "\n";

  perl 5.40.3   ISA=[Foo]             isa_foo=1  isa_nore=0
  PCL           ISA=[-norequire Foo]  isa_foo=1  isa_nore=1

`-norequire` is `parent.pm`'s FLAG, not a class: it means "do not `require` the
parents, they are already defined".  perl's parent.pm shifts it off the import
list.  PCL puts it in `@ISA`, defines a package for it, and emits

    (p-eval-always (p-require-parent "-norequire"))
    (p-eval-always (p-defpackage :-norequire))
    (defclass plc-bar (-norequire::plc--norequire Foo::plc-foo) ())

WHY IT LOOKS HARMLESS AND IS NOT.  Method resolution still finds `Foo`, so a
program that only calls methods prints the right thing — which is why no
runner noticed.  What IS wrong is observable and load-bearing:
  * `@ISA` has a phantom element, so anything that READS `@ISA` (introspection,
    `Class::ISA`-style walks, a test asserting the parent list) is wrong;
  * `->isa("-norequire")` is TRUE;
  * the C3 linearisation has an extra ancestor, so a diamond's MRO order can
    differ from perl's;
  * a package named `-norequire` is defined in the image.

BOTH SPELLINGS were probed: `use parent -norequire, "Foo"` (comma form) is
handled CORRECTLY — the emitted CL carries only the source echo.  It is the
`qw( -norequire Foo )` spelling, which is the one perl's own t/uni/method.t
uses (lines 175 and 179), that goes wrong.  So the fix is in whatever reads
`use parent`'s import list: the qw() path does not strip the leading `-`-flag
the comma path strips.

LAYER (CLAUDE.md 9a): `-norequire` is `parent.pm`'s own datum, so the fix
belongs in `lib/parent.pm`'s shim or in the generic import-list handling that
feeds it — NOT in a name test in `Pl/` keyed on the string "-norequire".
Check which of the two paths the comma form takes and route the qw() form
through the same one (rule 11).

BAR when taken: the reproducer matches perl on all three lines; the comma form
still works (probe it, it is the half that is right today); a guard row with
both spellings; `tools/ir-host-leak.pl --list` over perl's t/ shows no
`-norequire` token; corpus-diff; the gate; the full sweep and the uni/+mro/
companion legs if `lib/**` changed.

=== DONE (s470bo) ===

FIXED.  `_process_use_base`'s ad-hoc per-child scan is replaced by ONE
flatten, `Pl::Parser::_flatten_use_base_args`, which builds the import list in
SOURCE ORDER as perl hands it to `import` (barewords, `- word`, quotes and
qw() contents alike, reusing `_extract_parent_classes` for the quoted forms);
parent.pm's own rule then runs once over that list:

    if (@parents && $parents[0] eq '-norequire') { shift @parents; $norequire = 1 }

LAYER: the fix is NOT a third name test.  The string "-norequire" was already
in `Pl/Parser.pm` twice (a Word arm and an Operator+Word arm) â this removes
both and leaves ONE, at the point perl has it.  A `lib/parent.pm` shim was
considered and rejected for this task: `use base`/`use parent` is consumed at
COMPILE time to build the CLOS defclass for MRO, so a shim's `import` would
have to make @ISA changes at run time reach the class model â a different
mechanism, and much larger than the bug.

PROBED vs perl 5.40.3, before and after:
  use parent qw( -norequire Foo )   perl [Foo] isa_nore=0; PCL was
                                    [-norequire Foo] isa_nore=1, now [Foo] 0
  use parent -norequire,'Foo','Baz' perl [Foo Baz] â unchanged, was right
  use parent qw(-norequire Foo Baz) perl [Foo Baz] â was [-norequire Foo Baz]
  use parent qw(Foo -norequire)     perl DIES (require Foo.pm); the flag is
                                    honoured in FIRST position only, and PCL
                                    now leaves it in @ISA as perl would
  use base qw(-norequire Foo)       perl DIES; PCL stays lenient, as it
                                    already was for the comma spelling
  use parent qw(No::Such::Module)   perl DIES "Can't locate No/Such/Module.pm";
                                    PCL's p-require-parent is non-fatal BY
                                    DESIGN (an inline same-file parent has no
                                    .pm) â unchanged by this task, recorded
                                    here as a measured divergence

BIGGER THAN THE TASK KNEW: the flatten also fixes the PARENTHESISED list
spelling, which the old scan dropped ENTIRELY (it looked for Quote tokens
directly under the Structure::List and PPI puts a Statement::Expression in
between).  `use base ('Diamond_B', 'Diamond_C')` left @ISA empty, emitted no
defclass, and the program DIED at the first inherited method call.  **28 files
of perl's own t/mro/** are that spelling â found by the 1015-file emission A/B,
not by the reproducer.

BARS: host-leak census on t/uni/method.t 2 leaked symbols -> 1
(`op:-norequire::plc--norequire` 2 occurrences -> 0); corpus-diff over 111
files IDENTICAL for this change alone; the wide A/B's only diffs were
io/perlio_open.t (#1178) + uni/method.t + the 28 mro files.  Guards: three
transpile rows in `Pl/t/inheritance-01.t` and seven run rows in the new
`Pl/t/census-bugs-01.t`, inverse-verified.
subject: `use parent qw( -norequire Foo )` makes `-norequire` a SUPERCLASS: @ISA is [-norequire Foo] and `->isa("-norequire")` is true (perl: [Foo], false)
